label: Lookup
gloss: read the governed rule, reference table, or history the run needs
why: A record rarely carries everything the run needs to decide. A lookup reads a table the run does not own - the PO Register, the Vendor Master, a tolerance policy - and attaches the matching row to the record. At Beacon, INV-1 says it bills against PO-1; the lookup fetches PO-1 so the flow can see what was actually agreed.
cue: when a number or rule is about to be hardcoded in a step, that is a lookup waiting to happen - move it out where it can be owned and changed
task: Attach the purchase order INV-1 bills against: read the PO Register where the PO number matches, and name the result po.
notes: Match on: which field of the record equals which column of the store.
The result is attached to the record under the name you give it (as).
No match is not an error - the field is set to null, and a later step can test for that.

checks.label: INV-1 carries its PO (poTotal 1200)
checks.why: the lookup matched PO-1 in the PO Register and attached it as po
